assumptions: the gauge orbit is the affine R action generated by C and chi=t-tau is admitted on the full real lapse parameter without endpoint gauge obstruction in this toy model
the full-real-lapse integral is a distributional constraint projection eta_C=2*pi*hbar*delta(C), not a bounded idempotent Hilbert-space projector
the Berezin order (bar_c,c) and the corresponding antisymmetric matrix orientation are declared conventions
the +i0 prescription T->T-i*epsilon with epsilon>0 fixes the damped Fresnel branch before taking epsilon down to zero
the short-time statement is distributional on Schwartz test functions, not pointwise convergence of K_T
the finite toy normalization is not transported to gravity, minisuperspace, continuum ghost determinants, determinant lines, or arbitrary gauge systems

declared_model.endpoint_polarization: fixed x_i,x_f and fixed clock separation T=t_f-t_i>0
declared_model.fresnel_branch: K_T=(m/(2*pi*i*hbar*(T-i0)))^(1/2)*exp(i*m*(x_f-x_i)^2/(2*hbar*(T-i0))) with the branch continuous from T>0
declared_model.full_real_lapse_distribution: eta_C=integral_R d_lambda exp(-i*lambda*C/hbar)=2*pi*hbar*delta(C) in the declared distribution convention
declared_model.gluing_window: T_1>0,T_2>0; integrate the intermediate x in the same x-polarization

exact_calculation.gauge_orbit: t -> t+epsilon; chi -> chi+epsilon; epsilon=tau-t gives the unique slice intersection
exact_calculation.short_time_statement: K_T -> delta(x_f-x_i) distributionally as T down to 0 through positive times

exact_checks.statement: the affine gauge orbit shifts chi by epsilon and reaches chi=0 at one and only one epsilon
A_gh is antisymmetric in the declared (bar_c,c) order
Pf(A_gh)=+1 fixes the finite ordered ghost orientation
the two-slab phase completes to the single T_1+T_2 free-particle phase
squared Fresnel prefactors and the completed Gaussian integral equal the T_1+T_2 squared prefactor
the clock kernel delta(T-lambda) has the unique lapse support lambda=T; the full-real Fourier identity remains a distribution theorem guard

numerical_calculation.scope: bounded Gaussian-test diagnostic of the distributional short-time normalization; no numerical lapse, ghost, or continuum determinant integration

numerical_checks.statement: the declared +i0 free kernel approaches a Gaussian Schwartz test function at bounded small positive times

primary_sources.not_used_for: an absolute gravity or minisuperspace BFV measure
primary_sources.source: Henneaux and Teitelboim, Quantization of Gauge Systems (1992)
primary_sources.used_for: BFV gauge fixing, Faddeev-Popov determinant convention, and the distinction between a constraint distribution and a physical amplitude

primary_sources.not_used_for: a global Gribov theorem outside this explicitly affine gauge orbit
primary_sources.source: Faddeev and Popov, Feynman diagrams for the Yang-Mills field, Phys. Lett. B 25 (1967) 29-30
primary_sources.used_for: the determinant of the gauge variation as the finite ghost factor

primary_sources.not_used_for: a continuum determinant-line orientation or gravity contour prescription
primary_sources.source: Folland, Harmonic Analysis in Phase Space (1989)
primary_sources.used_for: oscillatory Gaussian/Fresnel kernels, distributional short-time limit, and composition of the free propagator

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: this toy gauge has exactly one intersection and determinant +1; it is not a Gribov census for gravity, compact gauges, or endpoint-restricted field theory
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the C flow shifts t by a free real parameter and chi=t-tau shifts with unit coefficient; the declared endpoint convention admits that full orbit

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the toy endpoint kernel is normalized by this declared distribution convention; eta_C is not asserted to be a bounded idempotent projector
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the lapse/group parameter ranges over the full real line, with eta_C defined as the stated tempered distribution and x endpoints paired with a fixed positive clock separation
theorem_guards.theorem: Fourier representation of the delta distribution

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the branch fixes the finite free kernel and its two-slab gluing. It does not determine a gravity lapse contour, Stokes data, Maslov data, or a continuum determinant line
theorem_guards.hypotheses: m,hbar,T_1,T_2 are positive and each T is continued as T-i*epsilon before epsilon down to zero; all slabs use the same branch and x polarization

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: K_T tends to delta(x_f-x_i) only as a distribution; no pointwise delta value or gravity endpoint contact term is claimed
theorem_guards.hypotheses: the statement is tested against Schwartz functions and interpreted distributionally as T down to 0 through positive times with the declared +i0 branch
